title: Bayer China Intern
summary: Professional corporate communication work produced during a Communications Internship at Bayer China, with a focus on long-form WeChat content, digital layout and publication-ready visual communication.
role: Communications Intern — WeChat layout, digital content production, visual hierarchy, publication preparation and supporting communication assets
tools: Xiumi · Adobe Creative Cloud · WeChat Official Accounts
demonstrates: Demonstrates professional experience working within an established corporate identity to produce clear, structured and publication-ready digital communication for real audiences.
sections: Project introduction

During my Communications Internship at Bayer China, I contributed to the production and publication of digital and visual communication materials across internal and external corporate channels. A key part of my role involved producing long-form WeChat content using Xiumi, translating supplied written content and visual assets into clear, structured and publication-ready articles while maintaining Bayer’s established brand identity.
My role

My responsibilities included WeChat article layout and formatting, Xiumi-based long-form content production, visual hierarchy and information structuring, image placement, publication preparation, selected section-heading development, social media graphic production, basic video editing and subtitle production, and promotional and internal communication assets.
WeChat content workflow
Supplied content and communication objective → content hierarchy → section structure → Xiumi layout → image and graphic placement → mobile-format refinement → final publication.
Content structuring

My primary responsibility was visual and editorial layout rather than writing full campaign copy. I also contributed to content structuring and selected section headings, helping improve clarity, flow and readability.
Published work

Selected published WeChat articles will be shown here as long-form mobile screenshots. Final screenshots and live article links will be added once the publication assets are prepared for the portfolio.
Other communication materials
Additional work includes social media graphics, promotional materials, long-form digital graphics, corporate gifts, event communication materials and selected video or subtitle examples.
Reflection

This experience strengthened my ability to work within an established corporate identity while adapting information for digital communication. It also gave me practical experience producing content for real audiences, preparing publication-ready assets and balancing visual clarity with corporate communication requirements.

title: SONY RE-COLOUR
summary: A colour-led Sony refresh using metallic gradients and sound-wave forms for a contemporary headphone campaign.
role: Research, colour exploration, brand development, campaign design, packaging design and motion experimentation
tools: Adobe Illustrator · Adobe Photoshop · Adobe After Effects
demonstrates: Explores how colour, motion and campaign applications can reposition an established identity while preserving its recognisable wordmark.
sections: Overview
Sony Re-Colour explores how colour alone can reposition an established global brand without altering its iconic wordmark.
Concept
The project develops a metallic, sound-driven colour system for a contemporary headphone campaign.
The Sound of O
The letter O becomes a visual device for sound, resonance, movement and immersive listening.
Applications
The identity extends across campaign graphics, packaging, product applications and motion.

title: 60 BPM
summary: A café identity translating a 60-BPM tempo into a calm, rechargeable brand world.
role: Brand strategy, identity, character, packaging and campaign design
demonstrates: Demonstrates the ability to extend one strategic concept across identity, packaging and campaign touchpoints.
sections: Overview

60 BPM is a speculative café identity built around calmness, restoration and recharging. The name connects sixty beats per minute with adagio: a slower tempo away from the anxiety and speed of daily life.
Concept

The central idea is rejuvenation through coffee. A logo combining a coffee bean and charger uses positive/negative charge symbolism, while the character Dagee helps carry the emotional tone into touchpoints.
Research & direction

Research covered café brands, merchandise, store atmosphere, logos, typography, menus, character design and relevant case studies. The intended audience includes students, workers, couples and families seeking a higher-quality leisure experience.
Identity system

Yorkmade and Montserrat establish the typographic contrast. Acid chartreuse, pink, black and cream create a distinctive but controlled palette, while tempo-based gradients expand the system into atmospheric campaign imagery.
Applications
The system extends across business cards, posters, coffee packaging, cups and sleeves, bags, merchandise, gift boxes and digital campaign applications.
Outcome
A complete identity presentation showing how one calm/recharge concept can remain recognisable across two-dimensional graphics and three-dimensional packaging mockups.
Transferable capabilities
Brief interpretation, concept development, identity systems, packaging, character design, campaign consistency and art direction.

title: Australian Light
summary: A research-led e-commerce redesign that transforms a static Australian photography gallery into a responsive, guided purchasing experience.
role: End-to-end UX evaluation, interface design, prototyping and front-end implementation
demonstrates: Demonstrates an end-to-end process from interface audit to responsive front-end implementation.
sections: Overview
An independent academic redesign of an existing Australian photography website, developed from interface analysis through high-fidelity design and a coded six-page responsive prototype.
Context / brief
The existing experience needed stronger navigation, clearer hierarchy, better product discovery and a more understandable purchasing flow while keeping photography visually prominent.
Research & references

Methods included existing-interface analysis, competitor review, a recorded cognitive walkthrough, mood-board development, iterative critique and qualitative feedback. The audit compared four photography-commerce websites and examined navigation, hierarchy, responsive behaviour and purchasing flow.
Key findings

The audit identified weak filtering and sorting, inconsistent grid hierarchy, limited product information, an overwhelming print-search process, unclear calls to action and limited recommendation support.
Development & iterations

Three visual directions led into sketches, low-fidelity wireframes and a Figma prototype covering homepage, search, product list, product detail, cart and checkout. Feedback prompted clearer cart states, checkout progression and refined scrolling/navigation behaviour.
Solution

The final responsive design uses photography-first layouts, guided product discovery and a clearer transactional sequence. A GenAI Print Finder proposal explored assisted discovery without claiming a production AI service.
Implementation

The front-end prototype uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript across six connected pages, including responsive overlays, cart state, form validation, checkout and order confirmation. The source documentation also describes persistent cart behaviour using localStorage.
Limitations & next steps

This remains a front-end academic prototype rather than a commercial launch. Back-end services, a complete product database and fully live commerce are outside scope; future work would expand the database and assisted discovery.
Transferable capabilities
Research synthesis, information architecture, responsive UI, prototyping, usability evaluation and front-end implementation.

title: Step / Motion
summary: A film and two-volume publication translating cyclical time through stairs, repetition, motion blur and material layering.
role: Filmmaking, sound, editorial design and bookmaking
demonstrates: Demonstrates cross-media storytelling through editing, sound, motion and physical publication.
sections: Overview
A paired exploration of translating time, tension and atmosphere between moving-image and physical editorial formats.
Step — moving image
Staircases, escalators and elevators recur as motifs of movement and time. Montage, repeated actions, overlapping moments, long exposure and motion blur contrast speed with stillness.
Sound & sequencing
Self-produced piano, recorded wind and footsteps, retained location sound and selected free sound-library textures build a restrained soundscape. Tutor feedback led to softer transition wind effects.
Motion — physical publication
A 10 × 15 cm, 16-page handmade artist’s book translates cinematic darkness and tension through black paper, tracing-paper layers, high-contrast imagery, restricted red/brown accents and sewn binding.
Outcome
Together the works demonstrate narrative interpretation, filming, editing, sound production, visual pacing, material experimentation and translation between media.
Transferable capabilities
Storyboarding, shooting, editing, sound, sequencing, material experimentation and editorial pacing.

title: Green Grid
summary: A community-garden app designed around coordination, information sharing and social connection.
role: Design and prototyping; contributions to research, coding transcripts, synthesis, personas and user flows
demonstrates: Demonstrates how qualitative findings can be translated into concrete navigation and interaction changes.
sections: Overview

Green Grid is a team mobile-app concept for community-garden members, developed through interviews, synthesis, personas, paper prototyping, high-fidelity Figma design and structured usability testing.
Research question
How might digital tools support organisation, information sharing and social cohesion within community gardens?
Research methods

The team used background review, semi-structured interviews, transcription, colour-coded thematic analysis, personas, conceptual modelling and user scenarios. Nine participants aged 18–56 were interviewed in Melbourne.
Synthesis

Three themes shaped the product: motivations and participation, organisation and coordination, and knowledge sharing. These findings informed task support, contextual plant guidance, plot management and community communication.
Audience & flows
Personas represented an existing member monitoring plants and a newcomer applying for a plot. Core flows include the garden map, plots, plant information, community, chat and profile.
Paper prototype
Diverge/converge ideation, brainwriting, reverse brainstorming and Crazy 8s led into paper prototypes and conceptual flow mapping before high-fidelity work.
Usability testing
Eight evaluation participants completed structured tasks. Testing revealed homepage density, unclear arrows, weak plot ownership states, unclear plot-application feedback and poor action visibility.
Before / after iteration

The team simplified the homepage, condensed weather advice, added profile imagery to owned plots, lightened unowned plots, expanded application confirmation, improved banner-arrow visibility and removed duplicated actions.
Final prototype
The refined prototype supports account/profile, garden news, interactive map, plot application and management, plant records, seasonal recommendations, forum, private chat and plant history.
Limitations & next steps
A real service would need configurable garden maps, stronger state feedback, help content, accessible non-colour ownership labels, privacy controls, moderation and transparent plot allocation.
Transferable capabilities
Interviewing, qualitative synthesis, personas, collaborative planning, prototyping, usability evaluation and evidence-led iteration.

title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Website
summary: A seven-page interactive website combining web design, motion and vanilla JavaScript into one connected Mario Kart experience.
role: Team Leader — homepage and explanation page design/development, team coordination, and shared CSS/JavaScript consolidation
tools: HTML5 · CSS3 · Vanilla JavaScript · Visual Studio Code · Google Fonts
demonstrates: Demonstrates collaborative front-end development, interaction design, responsive implementation and the coordination of a multi-page website system.
sections: Overview
A seven-page academic team website translating Mario Kart 8 Deluxe into a structured interactive web experience built with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript.
Direction
A dark interface with restrained yellow, red and blue accents carries the visual energy of the game across repeated navigation, cards, content modules and motion.
Structure
Home, Characters, Courses, Items, Battles, Quiz and Explanation are connected through one shared navigation and visual system.
Interaction
The source includes auto-scrolling galleries, mouse/touch course browsing, track pop-ups, hover discovery, scroll-triggered animation, video switching and a multi-step quiz.
Implementation
The site was built without a front-end framework. Shared HTML patterns, CSS and JavaScript coordinate page structure, responsive rules, visual motion and interaction state.
Outcome
The project strengthened the relationship between visual design and working front-end behaviour, including content structure, interaction and technical constraints.

title: EtheReal / Realm
summary: A virtual-idol identity expanded into a connected fan platform, social system and digital campaign.
demonstrates: Demonstrates how an expressive campaign identity can be translated into a structured digital product system.
sections: Overview
A connected speculative brand and digital-product project. EtheReal establishes a neon, pixel-led album identity; Realm extends it into a fan-facing social and commerce interface.
Brand chapter

The core ‘electronic butterfly’ idea frames idols as vivid yet distant presences mediated through screens. A pixel-led identity, member-colour system, logo, social campaign and album graphics establish the world.
Interface chapter
Realm translates the brand into app information architecture and UI components for feeds, member states, album content, merchandise, subscriptions, chat and profile flows.
Outcome
A brand-extension system that connects identity, campaign, interaction and commerce without inventing research claims not documented in the source information.
Transferable capabilities
Brand systems, UI components, information architecture, social content and cross-channel consistency.

title: N Exhibition
summary: An exhibition identity that blurs dream and reality through a fragmented N, collectible tickets and viewing filters.
demonstrates: Demonstrates concept development and the extension of a modular identity into participatory print and spatial applications.
sections: Overview
An identity for an interactive exhibition combining dream and reality through a modular symbol, hazy image treatment and collectible print pieces.
Concept
The N is divided into four quadrants representing a shifting relationship between dream and reality. Blur and softened edges create a hazy atmosphere.
Applications
The four-part system extends into collectible tickets, an N-piece postcard, Polaroid/photo filters and promotional/environmental applications.
Transferable capabilities
Concept development, modular identity, print application and environmental storytelling.

title: Modular Typeface
summary: A modular display alphabet extended from a small set of forms into objects, screens and cultural applications.
role: Module system, letterform design and applications
demonstrates: Demonstrates the construction of a repeatable typographic system from a restricted visual toolkit.
sections: Overview
A display typeface developed from a controlled construction system, progressing from graph-paper sketches to a complete alphabet and applied graphics.
System
Six documented modules generate the letterforms, balancing consistency with recognisable character shapes.
Applications
Alphabet, numerals, sample words and an applied skateboard graphic form the documented final set.
Transferable capabilities
Rule-based visual thinking, consistency, iterative refinement and typographic application.
